argument:
Netflix's 13% revenue growth and 33% operating margin are meaningful, but results were in line with guidance rather than a verified upside surprise. Full-year revenue of $51.0–$51.4bn and 31.5% margin are still forecasts. Current debt, FCF and content obligations remain unexamined, limiting a cash-supported valuation thesis.

The profitable revenue base rebuts an assertion of present operating failure, but cannot establish sufficient cash after content commitments. Competition and spending pressure remain scenarios, not observed new deterioration. Price below both averages with negative MACD and falling returns supplies no bottom confirmation. A buy would require more than management guidance and oversold RSI to resolve the conflict between solid operations and adverse trend.
key_points: Results met guidance; no incremental upside surprise is established.
Content-adjusted cash and obligations remain unverified.
Negative trend lacks a confirmed reversal.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull's 33% operating margin demonstrates profitability, but not cash available after content commitments and debt. Its full-year management scenario has not been delivered, and oversold conditions do not verify a recovery entry.
